findings.source: Vercel official Cron Jobs documentation, updated 2026-01-28
findings.evidence: Cron jobs run only on production deployments, Vercel does not retry failed cron invocations, duplicate delivery can occur, overlapping jobs can race, and Vercel recommends locks plus idempotency.
findings.why_it_matters: ARGUS must not equate configured cron state with successful persisted execution, and duplicate/overlapping runs could corrupt learning ledgers or double-consume API quota.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Add run_id, scheduled_at, started_at, finished_at, persisted_at, response_status, lock_acquired, duplicate_detected and output_digest to one non-critical research cron only.
findings.required_evidence: At least 7 days of scheduled runs with zero unexplained duplicates, zero overlapping writes, and complete CONFIGURED->DEPLOYED->INVOKED->SUCCEEDED->PERSISTED lineage.
findings.failure_condition: Any duplicate mutation, missing persistence acknowledgement, overlapping writer, unexplained gap, or cron path returning non-2xx.
findings.rollback: Remove instrumentation/lock wrapper and restore prior cron handler behavior; no model-state mutation involved.

findings.source: Probability calibration literature and ARGUS decision architecture
findings.evidence: Global calibration metrics can hide poor reliability on selectively accepted PRIME/VALUE cases; decision quality must be evaluated on the actual accepted subset with temporally separated calibration/test data.
findings.why_it_matters: ARGUS acts selectively, so trust must be earned where it chooses to act rather than on the full match universe.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Compute reliability bins, Brier, log-loss, calibration error and sample count separately for all predictions, accepted predictions, and each PRIME/VALUE/NO BET cohort without changing thresholds.
findings.required_evidence: Minimum 200 settled accepted selections for trend reading; prefer 500+ and multiple walk-forward windows before strong conclusions.
findings.failure_condition: Accepted subset is materially worse calibrated than full population, confidence intervals remain too wide, or results reverse across windows/leagues.
findings.rollback: Reporting-only experiment; remove cohort report with zero effect on production decisions.

findings.source: Bai & Jin, Conformal Selective Prediction with General Risk Control, 2026-03-25
findings.evidence: Selective prediction can explicitly abstain and control risk on trusted cases; recent work extends this with finite-sample risk control under assumptions such as exchangeability and studies shift-aware variants.
findings.why_it_matters: This maps directly to ARGUS NO BET: the scientific objective should be error/risk versus coverage, not simply maximizing the number of recommendations.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: In shadow mode only, generate empirical risk-vs-coverage curves using existing confidence/readiness scores and compare monotonicity across rolling time windows; do not implement conformal thresholds yet.
findings.required_evidence: Several hundred settled independent matches per broad market and stable risk reduction as coverage falls across multiple temporal windows.
findings.failure_condition: Lower coverage does not reliably reduce error/risk, group behavior is unstable, or exchangeability/shift assumptions are visibly violated.
findings.rollback: Discard conformal candidate layer; keep existing NO BET logic unchanged.

findings.source: Clegg, Song & Cartlidge, A market-calibrated accelerated failure time model for in-play football forecasting, 2026-05-15
findings.evidence: On 140 EPL matches, calibrating team strength to Betfair kick-off 1X2 and over/under prices was reported as the dominant driver of in-play predictive accuracy, with post-shot xG added as a time-varying covariate.
findings.why_it_matters: Before building a much larger live model, ARGUS should test whether market anchoring plus a simple interpretable state model captures most of the available signal.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: Build a shadow challenger that initializes pre-match team/goal intensity from de-vigged 1X2 + O/U market probabilities and updates only with already timestamp-safe live features.
findings.required_evidence: At least 1,000 independent matches across multiple leagues/windows, evaluated by time-clustered Brier/log-loss and calibration against both current ARGUS and market-only baselines.
findings.failure_condition: No reproducible OOS improvement, gains disappear outside EPL, or the challenger simply mirrors market prices without additive information.
findings.rollback: Delete challenger outputs; production live model remains untouched.

findings.source: Recent football prediction-market production-system research (Xu, 2026) plus established temporal-integrity principles
findings.evidence: The paper emphasizes an append-only frozen decision ledger and warns that recalibrating historical decisions with a current calibrator creates non-point-in-time records; the reported empirical sample is small and its profitability claims are not transferable.
findings.why_it_matters: ARGUS needs auditable frozen predictions and calibrator/model versions so post-hoc improvements cannot silently rewrite historical performance.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: For research decisions, persist immutable decision_timestamp, model_version, calibrator_version, feature_cutoff, odds_snapshot_id, market_snapshot_time, prediction_hash and settlement linkage.
findings.required_evidence: 100% reproducibility of sampled historical decisions from stored artifacts and zero records whose features/odds occur after the decision cutoff.
findings.failure_condition: Any historical record changes when current calibration/model code changes, or any post-decision information is discovered in the feature lineage.
findings.rollback: No rollback of immutable historical records; disable new ledger writer if schema errors appear and retain raw source snapshots.

findings.source: Xu, AI-driven Forecasting and Execution in Soccer Prediction Markets, SSRN 2026-07-28
findings.evidence: The work reports strong event-gated in-play outcomes but only around 100 settled matches and slightly negative closing-line value; these are author-reported production results and not independent validation.
findings.why_it_matters: The temporal-ledger concepts are useful, but copying betting-entry rules or profitability assumptions would be overfitting to a small, non-transferable sample.
findings.smallest_safe_experiment: None for real-money logic. If studied, replicate only as a shadow research benchmark after independent event-state data is available.
findings.required_evidence: Large independent multi-league OOS sample with pre-registered event gates, realistic latency/friction and clustered uncertainty.
findings.failure_condition: Any dependence on post-event leakage, unstable profit after costs, negative CLV without a separately verified timing edge, or failure outside the original competition/sample.

do_not_do: Do not increase PRIME confidence from small samples.
Do not add a large live model before market-anchored simple baselines are beaten OOS.
Do not treat cron configuration as proof of execution.
Do not restate historical predictions using current calibrators.
Do not infer edge from short-term ROI alone.
Do not change production in this dossier.
proof_required: Point-in-time immutable predictions and feature cutoffs
Clustered evaluation by independent match for live states
Rollback path for every experimental module
